mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT has risen for three consecutive weekly means (-36.6 to -30.4), showing restored out-of-home trip-making; transit and retail draw on the same discretionary-trip pool, so continued transit recovery mechanically lifts RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -36.6 at t-3w to -30.4 at t-0w while RETAIL_REC improved from -35.3 to -29.9
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean is at or below its last-28-day mean while TRANSIT keeps rising week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL has fallen by 2.8 points across the four weekly means (+10.9 to +8.1), meaning time spent at home is shrinking; each point of residential decline releases discretionary trips that surface in retail and recreation venues within roughly two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from +10.9 at t-3w to +8.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines over the next 28 days while RESIDENTIAL stays at or below +8.1 in every weekly print.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS jumped from -8.4 to +7.7 in the final weekly mean, crossing the baseline for the first time in the window; when outdoor activity exceeds baseline, adjacent commercial streets inherit pedestrian volume, so RETAIL_REC accelerates within one week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS weekly mean crosses from below 0 to above 0 (observed change +16.1 points at t-0w)
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS moved from -8.4 at t-1w to +7.7 at t-0w, the only positive park reading in the window
failure_condition: In the week following a PARKS print above 0, RETAIL_REC fails to exceed its trailing four-week mean.

mechanism_narrative: Commuting restoration requires WORKPLACES and TRANSIT to improve jointly; when both rise together the office-adjacent retail catchment refills, and the joint signal predicts RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks better than either series alone.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both improve on their prior weekly mean in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -27.4 to -21.1 and TRANSIT from -36.6 to -30.4 over the identical four weekly means
failure_condition: In weeks when WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both improve, RETAIL_REC does not rise above its prior four-week mean within two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has converged to within 0.7 points of baseline (-5.3 to -0.7), showing that stockpiling and necessity-only shopping are exhausted; the marginal shopping trip therefore reverts to discretionary retail, pushing RETAIL_REC up over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM weekly mean rises above -2.0 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose from -5.3 to -0.7 while RETAIL_REC stayed near -30 across the same four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean does not exceed its last-28-day mean while GROCERY_PHARM holds above -2.0.

mechanism_narrative: Under unchanged containment stringency, mobility converges toward a policy-set ceiling at a roughly constant rate; RETAIL_REC has closed 5.4 points in four weeks and, with no new restrictions, closes a comparable amount over the next four weeks, ending above its trailing mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved in every one of the last four weekly means: -35.3, -32.3, -31.3, -29.9
regime_hint: steady state reopening with restrictions held constant
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean is at or below the -32.2 average of the last 28 days without any tightening of the policy regime.

mechanism_narrative: The PARKS break above baseline combined with still-rising TRANSIT signals abandonment of voluntary distancing; a case resurgence follows within two to four weeks and forces re-tightening, which drags RETAIL_REC below its last-28-day mean by the end of the horizon.
candidate_trigger: PARKS weekly mean above 0 while TRANSIT improves in two consecutive weekly means
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS reached +7.7 and TRANSIT improved to -30.4 in the same week
regime_hint: post-relaxation surge risk within a reopening
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean exceeds its last-28-day mean while PARKS stays above 0 and TRANSIT keeps improving.

mechanism_narrative: The next four weeks contain the pre-Easter shopping fortnight, a calendar-driven spending peak in food and gift categories; this raises retail and recreation footfall above the March run-rate in weeks two and three even with no change in restrictions.
candidate_trigger: horizon overlaps the Easter shopping fortnight (weeks 2-3 of the four-week window)
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC t-0w mean is -29.9, the highest of the four weekly means, entering the holiday build-up
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean is at or below its last-28-day mean even though the horizon contains the pre-Easter shopping fortnight.
